reasons: The lake identity record verifies Arizona v. Johnson as a U.S. Supreme Court case decided on 2009-01-26, year 2009.
The lake citations list official citation 555 U.S. 323, parallel citations 129 S. Ct. 781 and 172 L. Ed. 2d 694, and vendor-neutral citation 2009 U.S. LEXIS 868.
The opinion frames the case as concerning police authority to stop and frisk a passenger in a motor vehicle temporarily seized after detection of a traffic infraction.
The opinion expressly states the rule in a traffic-stop setting and relies on Mimms, Wilson, and Brendlin, supporting Traffic Stops placement as progeny.
The opinion states that, for the duration of a traffic stop, police effectively seize everyone in the vehicle, including passengers.

The opinion holds that the first Terry condition is met when police may lawfully detain the automobile and occupants pending inquiry into a vehicular violation, without additional cause to believe an occupant is involved in criminal activity; a frisk still requires reasonable suspicion that the frisked person is armed and dangerous.
The opinion applies Terry's stop-and-frisk framework to a traffic-stop passenger.
The opinion says Mimms, Wilson, and Brendlin cumulatively portray Terry's application in a traffic-stop setting, supporting a Related (cross-doctrine) role for Terry Stops and Reasonable Suspicion.
The payload treatment fields match the disclosed lake treatment judgment: field_i_validity good_law, as_of_content 2009-01-26, as_of_treatment 2026-06-30, and varies_by_point false.
Lens A records the disclosed treatment-field match only; treatment/currency merits are outside this lens.
The lake identity record lists court U.S. Supreme Court and court_level scotus.
That disclosed identity supports the authority-weight label Binding — SCOTUS.
